reviews.title: Personal Excellence is the Ultimate Rebellion
reviews.text:
Politics is downstream of culture. And culture is downstream of character.

A free people must understand that public order is sustained by private order. The republic rests, in part, on whether enough people still possess the habits required for self-government. Discipline. Honesty. Restraint. Courage. Loyalty. Industry. Reverence. Self-command. These are not quaint private virtues disconnected from politics. They are the inner architecture without which liberty collapses into manipulation and appetite.

Rights must be exercised by people capable of handling them. Liberty requires a certain kind of human material. It requires adults. It requires judgment. It requires men and women who can say no to themselves.

Without that, freedom becomes self-destruction with a constitutional vocabulary.

In a culture of drift, order is defiance.

In a culture of excuses, accountability is defiance.

In a culture of cowardly euphemism, plain speech is defiance.

In a culture of softness, physical competence is defiance.

In a culture of dependency, self-command is defiance.

We must continue to attack the root system of decline. We must refuse the regime of mediocrity access to our souls. 

No one is coming to save us. Instead, we have to ask a better question, “What would excellence require of me now?”

You can begin now. Today. In the hour in front of you. In the obligations you already have. In the body you already inhabit. In the household you already lead or ought to lead. In the work you already do. In the promises you have already made.

Next step- download this app and get rolling. If any of this speaks to your soul at all, you will find a home here, and more importantly will be directly part of a world-altering effort. See you in there!

reviews.title: It’s alright
reviews.text:
If you get past the personality that is behind it and evaluate the application for what it is, at its cost point, it’s ok. It’s basically 50 dollars a month for some chat rooms, task management (I use the word “management” lightly) and an AI (based off of googles models) 

However when compared against what else is on the market, I don’t see the 50 dollars value. Maybe if this was brought to market 4 years ago? But today - not so much. You can get better AI features, better task management, and a better UI elsewhere. 

Some caveats: 

- the podcast is good 
- I like the branding 

The thing that made me leave: 

- Over promising on the “tech” (please stop saying you came up with new “tech” when it runs on googles infrastructure) - the features or “amazing things that are coming” are always “almost done”. However at 50 dollars a month, you should be getting a failure advanced application right out of the box. If you want beta testers, then I don’t think 50 dollars is a fair cost. I just got tired of the “we have the best thing in the world, but just wait a bit longer”. 

Unless you’re building from scratch which by all accounts isn’t the case, development with that amount of funding (including a beta testers group) should be much over streamlined. However, over the last 6-7 months, the only major changes to the end user was a slightly adjusted chat bot, social chat rooms, and of course a good podcast. 

This could always change. But currently, that’s the product.
